info.name: HustleHub+ API
info.description:
# HustleHub+ API, Part 2

Covers registration, login, authentication, role enforcement, gigs, bookings, transactions,
income, Admin role changes, sanitisation and rate limits. 171 requests in 14 folders, 1197 assertions.

The folders run in order and share one set of accounts:

1. Registration, successful. Creates the Clients and the Freelancers.
2. Registration, invalid scenarios. Duplicates, injection, weak input and oversized bodies.
3. Login. Valid and invalid credentials.
4. Authentication required. No token, a broken token and a forged one on the gig routes.
5. Role enforcement. Only the Admin changes a role.
6. Gigs. Create, browse, search, update, deactivate and delete, with ownership checks.
7. Bookings. Server side totals, validation, and who may read which booking.
8. Transactions. Read only records, visible to the parties and the Admin.
9. Income. The Freelancer income summary and who may read it.
10. Current user and role changes. Profile, user list, and a role change that takes effect at once.
11. Deleted gigs are gone and the records remain. Booked gigs are inactive, and bookings and transactions remain.
12. Sanitisation. Operator keys, dotted keys, deep nesting, markup in gigs and operator shaped ids.
13. Headers and CORS. Preflight from the client origin passes, other origins get no Allow-Origin header, and HSTS is on.
14. Rate limits. Failed logins and repeated bookings reach a 429 with Retry-After. Run this last, because it uses up limiter counters.

## Setup after cloning

Import two files from the `postman/` folder of the repository:

1. `HustleHub-Plus.postman_collection.json`, this collection.
2. `HustleHub-Plus.postman_environment.json`, the environment.

Select the **HustleHub+ Local** environment in the top right, then fill in the one
blank value, `adminPassword`. It must match `ADMIN_PASSWORD` in your `.env`, which is
the password `npm run seed:admin` gave the Admin account. `baseUrl` and `adminEmail`
already carry working defaults, so change them only if you changed your `.env`.

This collection stores no values of its own. Every configured value, and every token
and id the tests capture while they run, lives in the environment. That is why the
collection can be exported and shared without ever carrying a credential, and why
importing it raises no secret warnings.

## Before the run

1. Start MongoDB, then run `npm run certs` once.
2. Run `npm run db:reset`. This empties the database and seeds the Admin account, which
   the collection signs in as. The suite uses fixed email addresses, so it expects to
   start from an empty database.
3. Run `npm start`.
4. Run the collection with the Collection Runner.

The collection disables certificate verification for its own requests, because the
development certificate is self signed, so nothing needs changing in Postman settings.

To run it headlessly instead, use `npm run test:api`. That feeds `baseUrl`, `adminEmail`
and `adminPassword` in from your `.env` and needs no imported environment.

## The cast

Four accounts are created in folder 1 and reused throughout: two Clients and two
Freelancers. The Admin is created out of band by `npm run seed:admin`, because
registration refuses the Admin role and changing a role is itself Admin only.

## What is asserted

Alongside each request its own tests, every response in the collection is checked for
the security headers: a JSON only Content-Security-Policy, nosniff, a frame rule and no
X-Powered-By. Every response except a preflight is also checked to confirm it is JSON and that it never contains a password hash, a file path or a stack
trace. Folder 11 confirms the suite deleted the gigs it should delete, and that bookings and transactions remain.

The `npm run test:api` script also writes `postman/reports/newman-report.html` and `newman-report.json`, the full request and response record of the last run.
